claim: Revenue grew more than 50% year over year in fiscal 2026

base_rates.label: Base rate of yoy(revenue)[t] > 50% among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B

inputs.label: Revenue: every filer's row, by the first concept that has one

assumptions: Class: every filer in SEC's annual frames whose revenue in the test's base year was at least $100.00B (half the company's newest revenue, rounded down to 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten)

Each year t is a calendar-year frame: SEC places in it, for each filer, the fiscal year that best fits the calendar year; t-1 is the frame a year earlier, and the two periods must end a whole number of years apart.
Frames carry no filing date: a value restated later is the restated value.
The company itself is not counted: the rate is of the other filers of the class, and the years in which the test held for the company are listed apart.

A filer in the class in the base year with no value in year t (it was bought, went under, stopped filing, or changed its tags) is in the class but not computable: the rate is of the filers that can still be read.
A parent and a subsidiary that both file are two filers; a filer that reports in another currency is in no USD frame.
The SIC code is the filer's code today, not the code it had in year t.
base_rates.reading: Among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B (the company left out), yoy(revenue)[t] > 50% held in 4 of 366 company-years from 2011 to 2025; of the 4 that held and could be read a year later, 0 still held.

base_rates.class_definition: every filer in SEC's annual frames whose revenue in the test's base year was at least $100.00B (half the company's newest revenue, rounded down to 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten)
